text: A k=16 categorical Factorization Machine trained with Adam at lr=0.001 on user_id, video_id, author_id, tab, and duration_bucket reproduces the official baseline within seed noise (primary 0.6018 versus 0.6016) and provides no measurable improvement over it.

Adding a 29-dimensional dense side-information head with standardized continuous quantities and leakage-safe video/author historical statistics to the categorical FM produces no measurable gain: the raw candidate scored 0.6016 and its 0.5 blend scored 0.6021, both within 0.002 of the official baseline.

A query-grouped LightGBM LambdaRank model using 66 categorical, continuous, and leakage-safe historical features is substantially worse as a standalone ranker than the FM incumbent (primary 0.5921 versus 0.6021); validation selected only a 0.1 tree weight, and the resulting 0.6029 candidate is within seed noise of both the incumbent and o

A shallow temporal outcome model using feed order, same-timestamp batch position, session position, and inter-impression gaps is substantially worse standalone than the trusted incumbent (primary 0.5635 versus 0.6029); blending it at validation-selected beta 0.5 yields 0.6033, only 0.0004 above the incumbent and therefore no measurable ga

Same-timestamp batch and session-order features have sparse ranking context in this split: only 5.91% of validation examples belong to multi-item timestamp batches, mean batch size is 1.06, and mean session size is 1.51.

Smoothed user-specific preference features for candidate video, author, tag, and content attributes, computed from full and recent training history, add no measurable ranking signal to the incumbent: the profile-only model scored 0.4848 primary, validation selected beta 1.0 (discarding the profile model), and the final 0.6034 score is onl

The failure of the user-preference construction is not explained by unseen validation users, since 98.41% of validation examples have seen users; however, exact historical user-video pairs cover only 1.62% of validation examples, limiting direct repeat-video preference evidence.
Four consecutive iterations have failed to improve the incumbent by more than the 0.002 seed-noise threshold, so the experiment series has reached its predefined stopping condition.
